skill.name: java-unit-test
skill.description: Generate automated Java unit tests with JUnit 5 and Mockito, following the project structure and existing test style.
skill.summary: Creates focused Java unit tests that cover business logic, boundaries, exceptions, and mock interactions.
skill.author: gavin-ali

content.value_statement: Java teams often need focused tests that match existing project style. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create JUnit and Mockito tests with practical mocks.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the class under test, public methods, constructors, and direct dependencies.
Plans unit tests for normal paths, branch conditions, boundary values, and exception flows.
Generates JUnit 5 and Mockito test structures that match common Java project layouts.
Recommends mocks, spies, argument captors, and interaction checks for external dependencies.
Organizes imports, test data builders, assertions, and test method names for maintainability.
limitations: It does not run the generated tests or verify build results by itself.
It needs source files and project conventions to produce accurate tests.
It focuses on unit tests, not full integration or end-to-end test suites.
Custom frameworks or unusual build setups may require manual adjustment.

use_cases.title: Create service tests
use_cases.description: Generate focused tests for Java services with repository, client, or cache dependencies.

use_cases.title: Improve branch coverage
use_cases.description: Add tests for uncovered branches, boundary inputs, and exception cases in business logic.

use_cases.title: Standardize team testing
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent JUnit and Mockito structure across classes and modules.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate JUnit 5 tests for this Java class. Follow the existing package, naming, and assertion style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single class with clear dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Add Mockito coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this service and create tests for success, validation, and dependency failure paths using Mockito.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a service with external collaborators.

prompt_templates.title: Improve coverage gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the coverage report and source class to add tests for uncovered branches and boundary cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request based on coverage results.

prompt_templates.title: Design maintainable tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this module, identify hard-to-mock dependencies, suggest small refactors, then create focused unit tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for design feedback and test generation.

output_examples.input: A payment service with repository and gateway dependencies.
output: A test plan covering successful payment, declined payment, repository failure, and invalid amount cases.
A Mockito-based test class structure with mocks, setup, focused assertions, and interaction checks.

output_examples.input: A coverage report showing missed null and empty-list branches.
output: Additional boundary tests for null input, empty collections, and dependency exceptions.
Notes about weak assertions and any branches that need clearer product behavior.

best_practices: Provide the source class, related interfaces, and one existing test for style reference.
Ask for behavior-focused assertions instead of broad object comparisons.
Keep each test independent, fast, and clear about the scenario under test.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for tests without providing the source class or dependency contracts.
Do not overuse Spring context tests when simple Mockito tests are enough.
Do not assert private implementation details that make tests fragile.

faq.question: Does this skill support JUnit 4?
faq.answer: It is written for JUnit 5, but it can adapt when the project clearly uses JUnit 4.

faq.question: Can it mock static methods?
faq.answer: It recommends refactoring static calls first. Static mocking is suggested only when the project already supports it.

faq.question: Will it run the tests?
faq.answer: No. It generates and reviews test code, but test execution depends on the host tool and project setup.

faq.question: What files should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the class under test, direct dependencies, related domain objects, and existing tests when available.

faq.question: Can it improve coverage reports?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the coverage gaps, and it can propose tests for uncovered branches and boundaries.

faq.question: Does it create integration tests?
faq.answer: Its main focus is unit testing. It may suggest integration tests for critical contracts when needed.
